reason_empty: unknown model in request: llama-server b11755 single-model mode ignores the request 'model' field entirely and answers 200 on every endpoint probed (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /completion, /completions, /v1/responses, /responses, /v1/messages, /apply-template, /detokenize, /v1/chat/completions/input_tokens, /responses/input_tokens, /v1/messages/count_tokens, /tokenize; also model field given as number/null/array/absent). There is no error body to sign: the fault is silent success (predicate clause e requires status >= 400).

/models load/unload on single-model server: POST /models/load, POST /models/unload, POST /models, GET /models/<id> all answer the generic 404 body {"error":{"message":"File Not Found","type":"not_found_error","code":404}} (server-http.cpp:199-207). That whole body occurs verbatim in SKILL.md at base 1560e4d8 (row 'llama.cpp's normal root 404'), so any substring also occurs at base: clause b fails (scratch counter run B confirms: R26TestFNF404 -> b_new_at_base).

router-mode literals in server-models.cpp ("model is already running", "model is not found", "model is not loaded", "model is not running", "model must be a non-empty string", "request cancelled by a stop while the model was loading"): all lives inside router-only handlers (server.cpp:231-275 register them only when is_router_server). The counter's launches always pass -m <model> (fixture/missing/junk), which forces single-model mode; the counter can never exercise router mode, so the channel text for any trigger is the 404 envelope and never contains these literals (scratch counter run C confirms: R26TestRouterNF passes all static checks including d_in_source, live run shows 404, e_signature_seen false).

'Loading model' 503 window: the body {"error":{"message":"Loading model","type":"unavailable_error","code":503}} is already documented at base (SKILL.md S035/S036 rows, corpus/knowledge/llamacpp-loading-lifecycle.md) so clause b fails; additionally the counter's http channel calls wait_ready (polls /health until 200) before sending the trigger request, so a trigger can never observe the pre-ready 503 window (startup channel requires non-zero exit, which a successful launch does not produce).
